hero.eyebrow: For frontend teams that want to take back control of their architecture.
hero.pitch1: An architecture audit isn't another report to file away.
hero.pitch2: It's the clarity your team needs to stop being held hostage by its own codebase.

pain.title: Sound familiar?
items: Nobody really knows why certain decisions were made.
Every new feature takes twice as long as it should.
New developers take weeks to become productive.
Technical debt keeps piling up, but nobody knows where to start.

sample.title: What you actually receive.
sample.subtitle: Excerpt from an audit report — fictional data for illustration purposes.
sample.reportMeta: Prepared by Massimo Russo · Structure offer

issue1.text: State management coupled to components — no separation of concerns in the billing module.

issue2.text: Props drilling across 4 levels in dashboard components — brittle and hard to maintain.

issue3.text: No documented naming conventions for shared components.

sample.reco1: Extract business logic into dedicated composables — estimated 40% reduction in cyclomatic complexity.
sample.reco2: Introduce a Pinia store for the billing module with typed actions and immutable state.
sample.reco3: Define and document naming conventions in a shared ADR with the team.
sample.watermark: Fictional document for illustration purposes · massimorusso.io

cred.title: Real-world experience
cred.p1: 14 years building and structuring complex frontends for organizations that couldn't afford to get it wrong.
cred.p2: Air Canada, Fonds FTQ, Porsche, Férique, Intact — demanding contexts, teams of all sizes, different stacks. Every time, the same observation: what slows teams down isn't a lack of technical skill. It's the absence of clear decisions — documented, and understood by everyone.
cred.p4: I don't write theoretical reports designed to impress. I deliver concrete, prioritized recommendations I'd apply myself if I joined your team the next day.
cred.badge: Stack agnostic. Vue, React, Angular, Nuxt, Next — whatever the framework. Architecture problems all look the same.

hero.title: Services
hero.description: I support companies on frontend architecture, stack modernization (Vue/Nuxt) and technical decision support : with a pragmatic approach to AI when it brings real value.

process.title: How I work
process.description: A structured and collaborative approach to reduce uncertainty, clarify options and secure technical decisions.

discovery.title: Scoping & context
discovery.description: Understanding the challenges, constraints (legacy, team, delivery) and decisions to be made. Clarifying objectives and success criteria.

design.title: Analysis & options
design.description: Targeted audit, risk mapping, identification of realistic options and their trade-offs (cost, timeline, maintenance, performance).

development.title: Actionable recommendations
development.description: Proposal of a strategy (migration, target architecture, safeguards) and a concrete plan: quick wins, milestones and documented decisions.

optimization.title: Support & follow-up
optimization.description: Regular sessions, architecture reviews, support for Tech Leads/CTOs, and adjustments based on field feedback.

consulting.title: Frontend architecture
consulting.description: Architecture audits, target trajectories and modernization strategies for complex frontends : with explicit trade-offs, long-term clarity and controlled migrations (especially Vue/Nuxt).

workshops.title: Consulting & decision support
workshops.description: External advisory support to clarify, prioritize and arbitrate high-impact technical decisions: architecture choices, strategic options and long-term direction.

audit.title: Pragmatic AI usage
audit.description: Identification of meaningful AI use cases and integration paths into existing systems : with measurable value, explicit risks and no unnecessary complexity.

cta.description: Let's discuss your context, your constraints and the technical decisions to secure. I'll propose a clear and realistic plan.
